name: Bagisto
title: Bagisto SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Bagisto: 22 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; coupons, pages, payment methods and vendors are gaps. Setup and fixes.
lede: Solid core coverage: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Bagisto’s REST API. Bagisto chooses the channel by the request’s host, and takes locale and currency as headers.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, CMS pages, payment-method listing and vendors are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Bagisto channel

env.name: PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_URL
env.note: Your Bagisto URL. Bagisto picks the channel by matching the request’s host, so point this at the channel’s hostname. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_BAGISTO_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: A Sanctum token, sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_BAGISTO_LOCALE
env.note: Sent as `x-locale`; an unknown value falls back to the channel default.

env.name: PUBLIC_BAGISTO_CURRENCY
env.note: Sent as `x-currency`; an unknown value falls back to the channel default.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/bagisto-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_CHANNEL_ID`, which have no effect over Bagisto’s REST API — the channel comes from the host — and `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_SECRET` and `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_ACCESS_KEY`, which the connector’s source does not read.
backendSettings: Point `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_URL` at the hostname of the channel you want to sell from: Bagisto matches the request’s host against its channels’ hostnames, falling back to the first channel.
howItWorks: Bagisto has no channel header or parameter: it matches the request’s host against its channels’ hostnames. Locale and currency travel as the `x-locale` and `x-currency` headers, and signed-in shoppers carry a Sanctum bearer token. The storefront also ships a `/proxy/bagisto/*` route that forwards to `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_URL`.

faq.q: Can I run a Bagisto store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, CMS pages, payment-method listing and vendors are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Bagisto store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Bagisto?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/bagisto-connector`, set `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How do I choose a Bagisto channel, locale or currency?
faq.a: The channel by host: point `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_API_URL` at the channel’s hostname. Locale and currency by variable: `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_LOCALE` and `PUBLIC_BAGISTO_CURRENCY` travel as the `x-locale` and `x-currency` headers, and unknown values fall back to the channel default.

api.surface: The connector calls the `bagisto/rest-api` package’s plain-JSON REST API under `/api/v1`, checked against its tag v2.3.1, and not Bagisto’s GraphQL API or the API Platform package that api-docs.bagisto.com documents.
api.auth: The shopper signs in with `POST /api/v1/customer/login` (`email`, `password`, `device_name`), and the Laravel Sanctum token it returns is kept in the connector’s shared credentials and sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on every later call; there is no cookie, no CSRF token and no refresh token, so a 401 means signing in again.

calls.what: `GET /api/v1/products` with `query`, `category_id`, `url_key`, `featured`, `sort` and `page`; `GET /api/v1/products/{id}`, plus `GET /api/v1/products/{id}/configurable-config` for a configurable product’s variants
`GET /api/v1/categories` (with `pagination=0&status=1` to resolve a slug) and `GET /api/v1/categories/{id}` by numeric ID
`GET /api/v1/products` with `query`, `category_id` and `price=min,max`; `GET /api/v1/categories/max-price/{id}` for the price ceiling
`GET /api/v1/customer/orders` (with `increment_id` to find one order by number) and `GET /api/v1/customer/orders/{id}`

rules: Bagisto’s generic list controller turns every query parameter other than `page`, `limit`, `pagination`, `sort`, `order` and `token` into a `whereIn` on the table, so an unknown name is an SQL 500; the connector sends only those keys to `/categories`, `/customer/orders` and `/customer/addresses`, and resolves a category slug in the browser because slugs live in `category_translations`.

`/api/v1/products` accepts one `sort` token from a fixed list (`name-asc`, `name-desc`, `created_at-asc`, `created_at-desc`, `price-asc`, `price-desc`) and clamps `limit` to the store’s products-per-page setting, so the connector maps the storefront’s sort to one of those tokens and reads page size and totals from Laravel’s paginator `meta`, never from the size it asked for.
The cart has no ID: every cart route resolves it from the signed-in customer, so the Sanctum token is the cart identity and a shopper who is not signed in gets a 401.

Bagisto has no payment-methods route; the list arrives only in the response to `save-shipping`, and `save-order` fails unless `save-payment` has run first, so the connector places a cash-on-delivery order with the core `cashondelivery` method code.

An `etag` middleware answers a revalidating GET with 304, which the connector treats as an empty success rather than an error, and a 404 with no message is reported as the REST API package not being installed on the store.
